clue.text: A voracious reader

parts.note: a reader who devours books, pictured as a grub eating its way through the pages

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads constantly is said to be an insect larva that burrows through volumes.

clue.text: They cut dashing figures

parts.note: skates' cutting edges trace figures on ice, and dashing young men about town are also so called

explanation.definitionFit: Sharp cutting edges, and an old word for dashing young men.

clue.text: Exclusive treatment

parts.note: sounds like special privileged service, but means being shut out of a group

explanation.definitionFit: Shunning someone, banishing them from society.

clue.text: Best, strange as it seems

parts.note: the verb to best means to defeat, and an opposite-looking word has that same verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to defeat or get the better of someone.

clue.text: Go in for modified coverage

indicators.note: modified means the letters of go in for are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone decides to take up an improved insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Material laid over a building's top is its covering.

clue.text: Girl shows what she can get with publicity backing

parts.note: a girl can get herself a man, a suitor

indicators.note: backing means the word for publicity is read backwards

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A young woman finds out what promotion can win her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what she can get' is read literally: a girl can land a husband. 'backing' turns the publicity word round to sit last.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a female first name.

clue.text: Mother twice takes in the older variety of play

indicators.note: takes in means the doubled word for mother swallows another piece
twice means the word for mother is written two times

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: variety of signals a different arrangement of the letters of older

explanation.surface: Mum and Mum go to see an old-fashioned kind of stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges OLDER into ELODR, which the first MA of MAMA 'takes in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational dramatic piece with exaggerated characters is a kind of stage work.

clue.text: Fall behind it at the end of the day

definitions.text: Fall behind it at the end of the day

parts.words: Fall behind it at the end of the day
parts.note: putting the word fall after this one gives the close of the day, dusk

explanation.definitionFit: The dark period after evening, whose onset is called nightfall.

clue.text: Acting so strangely — from divine ignorance?

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of acting so appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone behaves oddly because they know nothing of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing the stance that God's existence cannot be known.

clue.text: Where one waits for Ena with a motor, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of Ena and a motor may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A woman called Ena sits waiting for her car to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles the eight letters of ENA and A MOTOR; 'for' and 'with' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room before a main one, used as a waiting area.

clue.text: Vessel showing its nationality?

parts.note: a ship shows its nation by having its ensign hoisted, so the drinking vessel is read as a banner plus a word for being displayed

explanation.definitionFit: A large jug for wine or cider is a drinking vessel.

clue.text: He may be booted on the stage

definitions.text: He may be booted on the stage

parts.words: He may be booted on the stage
parts.note: not kicked off, but wearing boots in a pantomime, as the clever cat of the fairy tale

explanation.definitionFit: Puss in Boots is the cat hero of a fairy tale often staged as a Christmas pantomime.

clue.text: Precise instruction to enforce payment

explanation.surface: A strict order to make someone pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate in every detail; and as a verb, to demand money owed, as a creditor would.

clue.text: Floods one sister with appointments

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a nun is a religious sister
dates are arranged meetings or engagements

explanation.surface: A busy nun is swamped with engagements in her diary.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood is to overwhelm with water, the same as to swamp.

clue.text: Gear-case?

parts.note: reads like a housing for a car's gearbox, but means a soldier's bag for carrying equipment

explanation.definitionFit: A cylindrical canvas bag in which a soldier or traveller packs their kit.

clue.text: A blockhead, our little boy is, in the middle class

parts.note: the head of the word block is its first letter, B
GEO is a short form of the boy's name George

explanation.surface: A family calls their dim son a member of the middle class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' is read as the head of 'block', its letter B, not a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for people of the propertied middle rank.

clue.text: I wish a student could translate this language

indicators.note: translate is taken in its sense of change or convert, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: L stands for learner, the plate a student driver displays

explanation.surface: Someone wishes a learner could render this tongue into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could translate' rearranges IWISHA plus L, the learner, into the East African language.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: In love and racing madly about — what chemistry is that?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: madly about means the letters of racing are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone besotted and rushing round wonders which branch of science this is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dove' as printed is an OCR misreading of 'love', the tennis zero. 'madly about' rearranges RACING into RGANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of chemistry dealing with compounds lacking carbon chains, as opposed to organic.

clue.text: Gave a shriek and scared me badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters of scared me are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone yelled and gave me a nasty fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out a loud piercing cry.

clue.text: Train regularly?

parts.note: reads like doing exercise often, but means travelling by rail to work every day

explanation.definitionFit: To travel daily between home and office, often by railway.

clue.text: Contents of the vendor's flat

indicators.note: contents of points to the letters held inside the run the vendor's

explanation.surface: What's inside the seller's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Level and smooth, with no bumps.

clue.text: Be dismissed but don't go?

explanation.surface: A player is given out but refuses to leave the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter who deflects the ball onto the stumps is said to have dragged it on this way and is out bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman who knocks the ball into his own stumps is out this way; otherwise it means continue playing.

clue.text: Dad holding a high card can solve all problems

indicators.note: holding means the word for father wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: PA is a familiar word for father
AN is the indefinite article, another form of a
an ace is the highest card in many games

explanation.surface: A father with an ace in his hand can sort everything out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: Goes hunting, we hear, for birds

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for hunting is pronounced like the answer in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: a hunter stalks prey by creeping up on it

explanation.surface: A predator heads out after some wading fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged wading fowl with large bills.

clue.text: Leaves producer to name theatre work

explanation.surface: A producer quits to give a title to a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree or shrub that keeps foliage all year; also the title of a 1930 Rodgers and Hart stage musical.

clue.text: Noblemen and king seen in a jumble sale

indicators.note: seen in places the king's letter inside the mixed letters
jumble means the letters of sale are mixed up

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Aristocrats and a monarch turn up at a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here 'jumble' mixes SALE, 'seen in' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the peerage ranking above viscounts.

clue.text: Sense of anxiety possibly Bag the third mate

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Sense of anxiety possibly Bag the third mate', is garbled by OCR; no parse of 'possibly Bag the third mate' gives ANGST and no source gives the true wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sense of anxiety possibly Bag the third mate

clue.text: Mother is upset over our love affair

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
is upset in a down clue means the word for mother is turned upside down

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum is distressed by our romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is upset' turns the mother word upside down, and 'over' puts it on top of 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for a romance, often secret.

clue.text: Vegetable to spoil the dressing

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
in military drill, dressing is aligning soldiers in a straight line or rank

explanation.surface: Ruining a vegetable by pouring the sauce over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' wants to be salad dressing; in drill, dressing the ranks means straightening them into a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A large green squash grown in British gardens.

clue.text: A glass ship

explanation.definitionFit: A tall glass for sherry or beer; also a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel.

clue.text: Stop side replacing good man

indicators.note: re-placing the letters of side means putting them in a new order

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Halt the team when a better player is brought on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges SIDE into DESI, followed by ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or refrain from doing something.

clue.text: Private accommodation?

parts.note: a private is a common soldier, so this is where such soldiers are housed rather than a personal home

explanation.definitionFit: Buildings where soldiers are lodged.
